title: Combined Burst Mode versus Torsional Mode Phacoemulsification for Patients with Hard Nuclear Cataracts: A Prospective Comparative Cohort Study

license.statement: CC BY-NC 4.0 via Dove Medical Press terms (article <license>); not CC BY or CC0, so the record is private

indication: Age-related cataract with Emery-Little nuclear grade III-V (white cataract, previous eye surgery, corneal pathology, uveitis, Fuchs dystrophy and glaucoma excluded; preoperative ECD above 1200 cells/mm2); subgroups by nuclear grade III (moderate) and IV-V (severe)

groups.description: Group A: phacoemulsification in combined burst mode (burst torsional + burst longitudinal ultrasound, Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision; nuclear grade III subgroup (40 eyes, Table 2)

Group A: phacoemulsification in combined burst mode (burst torsional + burst longitudinal ultrasound, Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision; nuclear grade IV-V subgroup (41 + 19 eyes, Table 2)
Group B: phacoemulsification in continuous (linear) torsional mode (Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision; nuclear grade III subgroup (46 eyes, Table 2)
Group B: phacoemulsification in continuous (linear) torsional mode (Centurion), divide and conquer, 2.2 mm incision; nuclear grade IV-V subgroup (41 + 20 eyes, Table 2)

exclusions.what: Table 2 'Pre-op ECD' for whole groups A and B
exclusions.reason: Follow-up ECD is reported only by nuclear-grade subgroup; the subgroup series with their own pre-operation reference are used

notes: Both phacoemulsification modes are routine settings of the same commercial platform, chosen by the surgeon's routine practice without randomization or an investigational agent: all groups are control-role; nuclear-grade subgroups (predefined baseline condition) are separate control groups.
Values are mean changes from the subgroup's own pre-operation ECD (value_kind ecd_change with reference_cell).
